newsitem.title: USA: Staples, Office Depot to pursue merger.
newsitem.headline: Staples, Office Depot to pursue merger.

text.p: Staples, Inc. and Office Depot Inc. said Monday they will fight the government's attempt to block the proposed $4 billion merger of the office products supply giants.
The companies also said they will seek an expedited court hearing in the case, contending that a union of the companies will result in lower prices for consumers.

"We believe an unbiased court of law will understand the merits of our case. The FTC clearly lacks an understanding of the office products industry," Staples Chief Executive Officer Thomas Stemberg said in a statement.
He said the company to be created by the merger would have less than a 6 percent market share in the fragmented $185 billion office products industry.

The Federal Trade Commission last week rejected the merger for the second time, arguing that it would raise price on office products across the country. After the government rejected the merger last month, the two companies negotiated a plan to divest 63 stores to rival OfficeMax Inc.
The latest 4-1 decision set the stage for the FTC to go into Federal District Court to block the merger.
The companies said they will seek the hearing to resolve the issue before the merger proposal expires on May 31.
In defending their proposed transaction, Staples and Office Depot said that virtually all of the products they sell can be found at numerous other types of stores.
In addition to contending their union would lower prices, the two companies said they anticipate increased employment at the combined firm and more opportunities for international expansion.

The companies released their statement after the stock markets closed. Shares of Staples rose 75 cents to $22.625 on Nasdaq, while Office Depot rose $1 to close at $14 per share on the New York Stock Exchange.
